questions.prompt: A third of your class failed the midterm despite attending every lecture. Walk through how you would diagnose the problem and adjust your teaching for the rest of the semester.
Describe how you would design a new elective course from scratch, from proposal to first delivery, in a department that follows outcome-based education.
Two of your strongest students accuse each other of plagiarism on a joint project. Explain the process you would follow and the principles that guide it.
Your department asks you to raise student engagement in a large 200-person introductory course. What specific changes would you make and how would you measure whether they worked?
A student with a documented disability requests accommodations that seem to conflict with a core assessment requirement. How do you respond?
Explain how you keep your course material current in a fast-moving field while keeping the workload realistic for students and for yourself.
Based on the attached course outline, draft a week-by-week teaching plan for the first six weeks, including one formative assessment checkpoint.
Design the grading scheme for this course. Justify the weight you give to exams, projects, and participation, and explain how you guard against grade inflation.
A key topic in this course is one you have not taught before. Describe concretely how you would prepare to teach it at the required depth within one month.
Describe how you would supervise a final-year project group whose topic overlaps this course, from scoping to final evaluation.
The department wants this course to include an industry-linked component. Propose one that is realistic for the stated class size and explain the logistics.
Identify the two biggest risks to student success in this course based on the outline, and describe the early-warning signals you would monitor for each.

dimensions.label: Structure
dimensions.description: The response is organised, sequenced, and complete.

dimensions.label: Reasoning
dimensions.description: Decisions are justified with cause-and-effect thinking.

dimensions.label: Domain correctness
dimensions.description: The response uses correct academic practice and terminology.
